paper.title: Distributed Learning Over Markovian Fading Channels for Stable Spectrum Access

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-user spectrum access over restless unknown Markovian (FSMC) channels with user-dependent rates; regret w.r.t. stable matching
unmapped: M users (agents) and K >= M channels; each user's rate on each channel is a finite-state irreducible aperiodic Markov chain, independent across user-channel pairs, evolving regardless of actions (restless)
Rates (means) differ across users; all entries of expected-rate matrix U are distinct (unique stable matching)
Comparator is the stable matching allocation (not the optimal matching), with weak regret against a genie knowing only means
Channel states observed via carrier sensing regardless of collisions; collisions yield zero reward
Algorithm uses parameter L depending on Markov chain constants (eigenvalue gap, state values, stationary distribution) and epsilon; uses opportunistic CSMA backoff signalling between users
settings.definition_quote: we define the regret for policy $\phi$ as the loss in the expected aggregated data rate with respect to the stable matching solution that uses the true expected rates: r_\phi(t) \triangleq t \cdot \sum_{i=1}^M \mu_{i,S(i)} - \mathbb{E}_\phi [\sum_{n=1}^t \sum_{i=1}^M X_{i,\phi_i(n)}(n) ].

bound.expression_latex: A_{\max}(\sum_{i,k}(\lfloor \log_4(3A_{i,k}\log t+1)\rfloor+1)) + \sum_{i,k}[(4A_{i,k}\log t+1+M^{i,k}_{\max}(\lfloor\log_4(3A_{i,k}\log t+1)\rfloor+1))(\mu_{i,S(i)}+\mu_{S^{-1}(k),k}-\mu_{i,k})] + M^2 A_{\max}(\sum_{i,k}(\cdots)) + [2e\log(M+1)(\sum_{i,k}(\cdots))][\sum_j \mu_{j,S(j)}] + (A_{\max}+(M^2K+MK)\frac{6X_{\max}}{\pi_{\min}}\sum_j\mu_{j,S(j)})\lceil\log_4(\frac32 t+1)\rceil + O(1)

symbols.N: number of users M in the paper
symbols.n_O_sum: sum_{i=1}^M sum_{k=1}^K (floor(log_4(3 A_{i,k} log t + 1)) + 1), with A_{i,k} = max{2/I, D^{(max)}_{i,k}} if k in G_i else max{2/I, 4L/Delta_min^2}
symbols.R_explore: sum_{i,k} (4 A_{i,k} log t + 1 + M^{i,k}_max (floor(log_4(3A_{i,k} log t+1))+1)) * (mu_{i,S(i)} + mu_{S^{-1}(k),k} - mu_{i,k}); M^{i,k}_max is the max mean hitting time
symbols.mu_SM: sum_j mu_{j,S(j)}, total expected rate of the stable matching
symbols.X_max: maximal cardinality of the Markov chain state spaces
symbols.pi_min: minimal stationary probability over all states, users, channels
symbols.C_0: constant independent of t (the O(1) term)

conditions: rates are finite-state irreducible aperiodic Markov chains, independent across user-channel pairs
all entries of the expected rate matrix U are distinct
tuning: exploration condition T^O_{i,k}(t) > max{D_hat_{i,k}(t), 2/I} log t

source.label: th:regret
source.quote: Assume that the proposed DSSL algorithm is implemented and that the assumptions on the system model described in Section \ref{sec:problem} hold. Then, the regret at time $t$ is upper bounded by: r(t) \leq A_{\max} \cdot (\sum_{i=1}^{M} \sum_{k=1}^{K} (\lfloor \log_4(3A_{i,k}\log(t)+1) \rfloor +1) ) + \sum_{i=1}^{M} \sum_{k=1}^{K} [( 4A_{i,k} \cdot \log(t) + 1 + M_{\max}^{i,k}(\lfloor \log_4(3A_{i,k}\log(t)+1) \rfloor +1 ) ) \cdot ( \mu_{i,S(i)} + \mu_{S^{-1}(k),k} - \mu_{i,k} ) ] + M^2 \cdot A_{\max} \cdot (...) + ... +O(1)

results.notes: Regret is t*sum of stable-matching means minus expected realized rewards (weak regret vs stable matching, not optimal matching); quantity set to 'other' and comparator approximated as best_fixed_action. Expression compresses the double sums into declared symbols; T denotes current time t. Paper's M (users) mapped to N.

symbols.Delta_U: paper's Delta_min: in the benchmark, difference in rates between the M-th and (M+1)-th best channels

conditions: benchmark setting: equal rates among users (rates vary only across channels)

source.label: th:regret
source.quote: In contrast, under DSSL, the regret scales as $O((\frac{1}{(\Delta_{\min})^2}+MK)\log(t))$ due to the novel algorithm design that explores every channel according to its unique adaptive exploration rate

results.notes: Informal scaling consequence of Theorem 1 stated in the discussion after the theorem, for a special benchmark case; dependence on Markov constants suppressed.
